# Pinned local calculation engines

The static release includes these sources, so deterministic calculations do not require a CDN or npm installation. No mandatory paid API is used.

* `astronomy.js`: Astronomy Engine 2.1.19, MIT, Don Cross. Exact upstream Git blob `6b73063bbc90bafe1ad9a712cfd9e9b958a54d60`, [source](https://github.com/cosinekitty/astronomy/blob/v2.1.19/source/js/esm/astronomy.js). Reused from the existing Astrology Workbench and verified against that upstream blob. License retained in the header. 412,025 uncompressed bytes; shared module loading deduplicates it across sky, events and orbits.
* `satellite/` and `satellite.esm.js`: satellite.js **7.1.0**, MIT, pinned [commit `582a72ecf9cb22fd3c210f1e497d8565517f1d6d`](https://github.com/shashwatak/satellite-js/tree/582a72ecf9cb22fd3c210f1e497d8565517f1d6d/src). The 21 non-WASM TypeScript files were retrieved through GitHub on 2026-10-05 and each Git blob verified before compilation. Native ESM was produced with Node.js **v24.19.0**, `node:module.stripTypeScriptTypes(source, {mode: 'transform'})`. The only source alteration removes `export * from './wasm/index.js'` from the entry point; no calculation algorithms changed. Optional WASM is neither vendored nor loaded. `satellite/upstream.json` records original blob hashes and emitted SHA-256 hashes; `satellite-LICENSE.md` is unchanged upstream MIT text (Git blob `a2d06db2aa2dd1e9859015d9e0ce801ffae23a1a`). Runtime JS totals **64,091 raw bytes** versus the prior 4.1.4 sources' 89,224; formatting/type stripping contributes to this reduction, so it is not a load-speed measurement. See [satellite methods and measured calculation costs](../docs/satellite-nearby-methods.md).

To reproduce the satellite source graph, retrieve each `source` path in `satellite/upstream.json` at that commit, verify its Git blob SHA-1 (`SHA1("blob " + byteLength + NUL + source)`), remove only the documented optional WASM export, and run the pinned Node transform above. Write each listed `output` and compare its SHA-256 to the manifest. Browser delivery uses the emitted `.js` files directly; neither Node nor a compilation step is required for GitHub Pages. Independent Vallado propagation fixtures are exercised by `node tests/satellites-nearby.mjs`.

Live satellite/aircraft data is optional and has separate freshness, privacy and availability constraints. This release does not promise completely offline first navigation; it works from any static host with these files available.
